t:
(a) Increase.—Section 327(d)(1) of title 37, United States Code, is amended by striking “$2,500” and inserting “$10,000”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall take effect on October 1, 2006, and shall apply to agreements entered into or revised under section 327 of title 37, United States Code, on or after that date.

fable.w: The section only raises a dollar cap in a military pay statute from $2,500 to $10,000 and sets an effective date. The tempting reading is that the word "agreements" signals outside-party involvement, but these are individual bonus agreements under the pay statute, not consultation with outsiders on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall apply to agreements entered into or revised under section 327 of title 37, United States Code, on or after that date

opus.w: This section only raises the bonus amount in 37 U.S.C. 327(d)(1) and sets when the change takes effect. The word "agreements" refers to individual service members' bonus agreements, which are benefit arrangements. It does not mean anyone outside the government takes part in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: Section 327(d)(1) of title 37, United States Code, is amended by striking “$2,500” and inserting “$10,000”.
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that the word "agreements" points to a deal or negotiation between the government and someone outside it. That reading fails. These agreements are military service members' transfer-bonus agreements under 37 U.S.C. § 327, and they work like signing up for a benefit. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted on a federal decision. The section only raises a dollar cap and sets an effective date. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends a statutory dollar limit and sets an effective date for that amendment. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The reference to 'agreements' is incidental to the scope of the amendment's application, not a description of a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 327(d)(1) of title 37, United States Code, is amended by striking “$2,500” and inserting “$10,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "agreements entered into" implies negotiation with outside parties (e.g., contractors or states), which could involve participation. However, the text itself only amends a dollar limit and sets an effective date; it does not describe the process of entering into those agreements, nor does it mandate any consultation, hearing, or public comment period regarding the agreements themselves. The section is purely administrative and financial.
